chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Salim, from Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had unlawful intercourse with a slave girl, then bought her, and claimed her son. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would not inherit from him.' Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child is for the bed (conception), and for the adulterer is the stone, and the child of adultery would not inherit except a man who claims a son of his slave girl.'

key_terms.الْحَجَر: The stone (referring to the stone thrown at the adulterer)
key_terms.الْفِرَاش: The bed (referring to the place of conception/marriage bed)

ai.seo_question: Does a man inherit from the son of his slave girl if he had unlawful intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific exception to the general rule that 'the child is for the bed' (al-waladu lil-firash), establishing that a man who commits zina with his own slave girl (ummu walad) and subsequently purchases her can claim inheritance rights from her son. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the ummu walad in Shia jurisprudence, where her emancipation upon the master's death or purchase creates a bond of nasab sufficient for mutual inheritance, distinguishing her case from other forms of illegitimate offspring.
